topic: GC never invents a ref transition
canonical_claim: GC never invents a ref transition; abandoned precommit cleanup is performed by the writer or its successor rather than by a synthetic GC event.

topic: GC condemnation marker is add-only
canonical_claim: The GC condemnation marker is add-only: GC may change `Clean` to `Condemned` and delete the marker after a confirmed body delete, but never changes `Condemned` back to `Clean`.

topic: blob `
canonical_claim: A blob `.meta` sidecar has only `Clean` and `Condemned` states; an absent sidecar reads as `Clean`, and the sidecar contains no token.; `MetaState::Clean` means the blob is referenceable and present, while `MetaState::Condemned` means GC found zero in-degree but the body remains present and may be resurrected by a writer CAS. Additionally, The condemned-state gate remains correct when the text codec round-trips `state`, `condemn_round`, and `size`, because dedup and GC branch on decoded fields and CAS-swap by etag.

topic: pre-precommit orphan manifest has no ref-log owner edge and is reclaimed by the
canonical_claim: A pre-precommit orphan manifest has no ref-log owner edge and is reclaimed by the orphan sweep, whereas a dangling precommit must first have its binding removed before GC can reclaim the body.

topic: Blob liveness is represented by a set of source edges
canonical_claim: Blob liveness is represented by a set of source edges; `precommitAdd` creates `+1` edges, owner removals create `-1` edges, `promote` creates no edge, and inline manifest entries create none.

topic: GC discovers the ref live set by listing `cas/ns/stream/`, joining opaque life i
canonical_claim: GC discovers the ref live set by listing `cas/ns/stream/`, joining opaque life ids to one catalog cut, and folding each admitted log only after its complete coverage is durable.

topic: implemented GC round is a single pass of 18 named phases ending in exactly one `
canonical_claim: The implemented GC round is a single pass of 18 named phases ending in exactly one `gc/state` CAS; the older `fold → retire → fence → recheck → trim` shape is superseded.; The GC log's `phase` column has these 18 execution-order values: `lease`, `pre_fold_ref_drain`, `heartbeat_floor`, `defer_decision`, `parent_seal_read`, `fold_ref_group`, `fold_seal_read`, `fold_ref_intake`, `fold_reduce`, `fold_seal_write`, `pending_deletes`, `meta_pool_wait`, `round_commit`, `handoff_reclaim`, `manifest_deletes`, `namespace_cleanup`, `ref_object_cleanup`, and `orphan_sweep`. Additionally, The 18 GC phases execute in this order: `lease`, `pre_fold_ref_drain`, `heartbeat_floor`, `defer_decision`, `parent_seal_read`, `fold_ref_group`, `fold_seal_read`, `fold_ref_intake`, `fold_reduce`, `fold_seal_write`, `pending_deletes`, `meta_pool_wait`, `round_commit`, `handoff_reclaim`, `manifest_deletes`, `namespace_cleanup`, `ref_object_cleanup`, `orphan_sweep`.

topic: `gc/state` is the durable round-adoption state and exactly one CAS per round pub
canonical_claim: `gc/state` is the durable round-adoption state and exactly one CAS per round publishes it; the fold seal records generation, parent generation, catalog-life coverage, source-edge runs, and condemned summaries.

topic: Condemned entries are stored as sentinel rows in the source-edge run
canonical_claim: Condemned entries are stored as sentinel rows in the source-edge run; there is no separate retired-list object and no run-file list outside the fold seal.; The 2-cursor settlement merge removes the separate `prior_retired` input: condemned rows are decoded from the prior source-edge run, settled at blob close-out, and emitted back at the blob's zero-sentinel key. Additionally, The retired-in-snapshot design stores condemnation state as `kCondemned` sentinel rows in the source-edge run and stores per-shard `condemned_summary` in the fold seal; the merge therefore uses two cursors instead of three.

topic: GC coordinator owns discovery, round visibility, the global fence, and generatio
canonical_claim: The GC coordinator owns discovery, round visibility, the global fence, and generation advancement; reducers own disjoint digest shards, and pure-carry shards copy parent run references with zero run I/O.

topic: planned incarnation-aware fold treats a sealed/live incarnation mismatch as an a
canonical_claim: The planned incarnation-aware fold treats a sealed/live incarnation mismatch as an absent prior cursor, restarts at `folded_cursor = 0`, drops carried edges from the old incarnation, and stamps the live incarnation into the new seal.

topic: Before D1, `discoverUniverse` enumerated `registry
canonical_claim: Before D1, `discoverUniverse` enumerated `registry.namespaces × shardsToVisit`, so GC fencing cost was proportional to namespaces ever created times `root_shards` and could mint fence-only manifests for absent shards.

topic: abandoned newborn is treated as an abandoned precommit and reclaimed by the exis
canonical_claim: An abandoned newborn is treated as an abandoned precommit and reclaimed by the existing `(writer_epoch, build_sequence)` watermark path; after it empties, tombstone reclaim handles its shard object.

topic: Successful copy-forward emits `CasEventType
canonical_claim: Successful copy-forward emits `CasEventType::BlobCopyForward` and increments `CasBlobCopyForward`; the old `(hash, t)` entry remains listed until exact-token settlement, while the new incarnation is protected from wrong-token deletion.

topic: GC min_ack semantics
canonical_claim: An ack-floor entry graduates only when `condemn_round < min_ack`, where `min_ack` is the minimum `observed_gc_round` among live heartbeats or live/expired-but-not-fenced heartbeats; terminated and fenced heartbeats are excluded, and if no live heartbeats exist then `min_ack = +∞`.

topic: ack-floor open ordering is claim heartbeat → load `gc/state` and the retired lis
canonical_claim: The ack-floor open ordering is claim heartbeat → load `gc/state` and the retired list → stamp the acknowledgement → enable mutations, and retired-list objects must be durable before the `gc/state` CAS publishes the round.; The GC publish-order invariant requires the retired-list runs for round K to be durable before the single `gc/state` CAS publishes `round := K` and `retired_refs`; refs and round are published together so round K always has a loadable retired list K.

topic: three-cursor merge graduates entries with `condemn_round < min_ack`, keeps entri
canonical_claim: The three-cursor merge graduates entries with `condemn_round < min_ack`, keeps entries at `condemn_round == min_ack`, spares entries whose in-degree recovers, captures a token for new zero-in-degree condemnations, and skips absent blobs.

topic: current retired-candidate set is stored as per-GC-shard artifacts using the stri
canonical_claim: The current retired-candidate set is stored as per-GC-shard artifacts using the strict `cas_retired_set` protobuf codec (`RetiredSetProto`, magic `CART`), with entries sorted by `(kind, hash)` and each entry containing `(blob_hash, token, condemn_round)`.

topic: retired-list and `condemn_round` protobuf fields are additive fields in the same
canonical_claim: The retired-list and `condemn_round` protobuf fields are additive fields in the same compatibility regime as `snap_attempt`; no per-object version integer is bumped, and future `compatibility_version` values fail closed.

topic: Discovery performs one paginated LIST of `cas/refs/` and ETag-diffs it against p
canonical_claim: Discovery performs one paginated LIST of `cas/refs/` and ETag-diffs it against per-shard folded tokens; backends with `supportsListTokens = false` use per-shard HEAD/GET and remain fail-closed and read-only.

topic: GC merge processes the prior snapshot run, sorted edge deltas, and prior retired
canonical_claim: The GC merge processes the prior snapshot run, sorted edge deltas, and prior retired run with three cursors sorted by `blob_hash`, emitting the new snapshot run, retired run, and delete list in one streaming pass.

topic: retired candidate with recovered in-degree greater than zero is spared and remov
canonical_claim: A retired candidate with recovered in-degree greater than zero is spared and removed from the retired output; the implementation emits a B170 recheck-verdict event with the recovered in-degree.

topic: retired candidate with zero in-degree graduates only when `condemn_round < min_a
canonical_claim: A retired candidate with zero in-degree graduates only when `condemn_round < min_ack`; a zero-in-degree candidate with `condemn_round >= min_ack` remains in the retired list.

topic: rebuild-history-guard
canonical_claim: A fold using an empty baseline must throw `CORRUPTED_DATA` when a discovered ref shard proves trimmed history: `journal.front().transition_version > 1`, or an empty journal with `shard_version > 0`. Additionally, `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD` reconstructs per-shard fold cursors and blob in-degree from owner shards and journals, and its baseline guard raises `CORRUPTED_DATA` when trimmed history cannot be accounted for.

topic: The baseline guard gates GC only
canonical_claim: The baseline guard gates GC only; it never blocks server startup or normal reads and writes, and a genuinely fresh pool whose journals start at version 1 passes.

topic: Rebuild edge accumulation is bounded by a memory budget
canonical_claim: Rebuild edge accumulation is bounded by a memory budget: per-GC-shard edges are sorted and spilled into temporary run segments, then merged into one run using the T2 streaming readers and `RunFileWriter`.

topic: The rebuild mints `new_round = max(observed_gc_round over all mount bodi
canonical_claim: The rebuild mints `new_round = max(observed_gc_round over all mount bodies, fence_round over all shards, and surviving gc/gen prefix numbers) + 1` so stale acknowledgements cannot float fresh condemnations past the floor.

topic: The rebuild's per-shard guard is stricter than a global empty-baseline c
canonical_claim: The rebuild's per-shard guard is stricter than a global empty-baseline check: it fires for any shard with no sealed cursor whose journal proves trimmed history, while a shard born after the baseline passes because its journal starts at `transition_version` 1.

topic: The raw rebuild API returns `RebuildReport` with `performed`, `refusal`,
canonical_claim: The raw rebuild API returns `RebuildReport` with `performed`, `refusal`, minted `round` and `generation`, counts for namespaces, shards, committed refs, live precommits, unowned-alive manifests, edges, and clamped shards.

topic: A deferred owner removal is conservative because the stale in-degree is
canonical_claim: A deferred owner removal is conservative because the stale in-degree is too high and can only delay reclaim, whereas a deferred owner addition is dangerous if a pending blob graduates from a stale zero in-degree snapshot.
